body.heading: The hidden cost of switching
paragraphs: Each time you jump from a task to a message and back, part of your attention stays behind, catching up. A day of constant switching can leave you busy, tired, and oddly unfinished.
Working on one thing at a time is not a moral stance; it is an efficiency one. The task gets your whole mind, errors drop, and finishing something completely becomes possible again.

body.heading: Make single-tasking easy
paragraphs: You cannot rely on willpower against a buzzing pocket. Put the phone in another room, close the extra tabs, and let people know you will be unreachable for a short stretch. Most things can wait thirty minutes.
Start with one protected block a day, even twenty minutes. Notice how the work feels: slower at first, then strangely calm, and often done sooner than the fragmented version would have been.

takeaway: Give one thing your whole attention for a short block, and let the rest wait.
